events.subtitle: 2026-only performance
events.factual_description: COTTON CLUB presents WEST ROAD BLUES BAND on September 30, 2026, with sets at 6:00 PM and 8:30 PM. The venue identifies the group as a pioneering force in Japanese blues, formed in 1972 around members including Takashi Nagai and Junshi Yamagishi, and notes that the band helped drive Japan's 1970s blues boom after opening for B.B. King in Japan and recording from 1975 onward. After suspending activity following Shinji Shiotsugu's death in 2008, the group returned for its 50th-anniversary period in 2025. COTTON CLUB states that the September 30 date is the band's only performance of 2026, made possible by U.S.-based guitarist Junshi Yamagishi's temporary return to Japan.

en.why_it_matters: This clears S because the context is much rarer than a routine legacy-blues booking. WEST ROAD BLUES BAND is foundational to the Japanese blues lineage, the current appearance follows a long period of inactivity, and COTTON CLUB explicitly says this is the band's only performance of 2026, enabled by Junshi Yamagishi's temporary return from the United States. In an intimate room, the surviving band's guitar-centered vocabulary and groove become a living piece of Japanese music history rather than nostalgia-by-default.
en.trip_verdict: S within Greater Tokyo/Kanto. Protect one of the two sets and cross Tokyo for it if Japanese blues history, guitar language and groove matter to you. It is a strong music-trip anchor because the band is only playing once in 2026, but it stops short of S+ because the event is not framed as a farewell, final reunion or otherwise singular endpoint.

es.why_it_matters: Cruza a S porque el contexto es mucho más raro que una fecha rutinaria de blues de legado. WEST ROAD BLUES BAND es una pieza fundacional del blues japonés, esta aparición llega después de un largo periodo de inactividad y COTTON CLUB dice explícitamente que será la única actuación del grupo en 2026, posible por el regreso temporal de Junshi Yamagishi desde Estados Unidos. En una sala íntima, su vocabulario de guitarras y groove funciona como historia viva de la música japonesa, no como nostalgia automática.
es.trip_verdict: S dentro de Greater Tokyo/Kanto. Sí protegería uno de los dos sets y cruzaría Tokio por esto si te importan la historia del blues japonés, el lenguaje de guitarra y el groove. Es una ancla fuerte para un viaje musical porque la banda sólo tocará una vez en 2026, pero no llega a S+ porque no está planteado como despedida, reunión final ni cierre singular de una etapa.
